recipes.name: Chef John's Crab Cakes
ingredients_raw: 0.5 teaspoon seafood seasoning (such as Old Bay®)

steps.text: Mix crushed crackers, mayonnaise, Dijon, seafood seasoning, Worcestershire sauce, egg, cayenne, and salt together in a large bowl. Add crabmeat and stir until combined but still chunky. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Sprinkle bread crumbs onto a plate. Shape chilled crab mixture into four small, thick patties. Coat patties completely with bread crumbs.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add crab cakes and cook until golden brown, about 4 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John's Crab Cakes
raw_recipe.description: Chef John's crab cake recipe makes perfectly seasoned crab cakes with minimal filler that are crispy on the outside and sweet and tender on the inside.

review.reviewBody: Excellent! If you are looking for a true Maryland crab cake, look no further. This is it! I have lived in Maryland, minutes from the Chesapeake Bay for 25 years, and this is practically identical to mine (I just use 12 crushed Ritz crackers, no bread crumbs), but I will try Chef John's version. I'm very lucky, get fresh crabmeat all summer and Old Bay is a must, if you can get it. You must try this recipe!

I followed this recipe with the exception of using Ritz crackers instead of Saltines. I also don't measure everything (like the mustard and Worcestershire sauce) but simply "eyeball" the quantity. I used fresh Dungeness crab, which has the best and sweetest meat in my opinion. While the recipe indicates 4 crab cakes for a pound of crab I found five or six would still provide a healthy sized crab cake. I fried the crab cakes in clarified butter. As Chef John said, these are basically just crab. I did find that chilling the crab cakes prior to frying helped to maintain their shape and keep them together. I served these with Chef John's Tarragon Aioli. Delicious and highly recommended!

Made this twice with left over king crab legs. One hack that helped to keep them together during the crumbing was using a slider patty ring (or open top biscuit cutter) and parchment. I would put the ring on the parchment square, sprinkle crumbs in it, add crab cake mix, press down and add crab cakes to top. When you flip it into the pan, you have more control.

Recipe is perfect - I used 9 ritz crackers instead of saltines. Refrigerated for 3 hrs. Did not put breadcrumbs on the outside; just fried in a cast iron skillet in butter. Awesome flavor!! Served with remoulade sauce.

As I sit writing this review my dear husband is jumping up and down. He said I hit one out of the park with these crab cakes. I substituted the half a teaspoon of Bichon mustard for a quarter of a teaspoon of hot sauce and a quarter of a teaspoon of yellow mustard. I also put the patties in my freezer for half an hour instead of chilling them for the full hour. We also like heat so I added approximately a quarter of a teaspoon to a half a teaspoon of cayenne pepper. The flavor profile of these is on point. I may add a few extra crackers just because they were a little flakier than I care for. My husband is looking forward to Future crab cake meals!!!! Make them you won't be disappointed!

There are flat out delicious. I did use ritz because it's what I had on hand, and added more old bay because we like it (3/4 teasp). But I'd make these as written too, and be thrilled with the results. Best crab cakes I've ever had!

Followed the recipe. Only had 9 oz of crab meat, 1 good sized crab I picked. So I made 2 cakes, split the recipe. Better than restaurant crab cakes by far. best we ever had. Not surprised, all my go to best recipes are from Chef John. Teacher, entertainer, chef. Bravo!

Broil them! Im born and raised in MD . I would add 4 crackers , double the Mayo and all the other ingredients except bread crumbs . I would add a pat of butter on each crab cake and broil until golden brown 😘

I used panko instead of breadcrumbs, which added a nice crunch to the texture. I found it necessary to add one more egg to the recipe in order to mold the crabcakes and not have them fall apart. I would suggest adding the extra egg; otherwise an excellent recipe - the best I have found. I also used Chef John's recipe for remoulade sauce, which went very well with the crabcakes.
Really like this crab cake recipe. Substituted club crackers for the saltines and panko for the bread crumbs. Also added chopped green onion to the mixture.

I have tried to make crab cakes in the past with less than ideal results. This recipe was delicious and easy. I halved it because I had 1/2 pound of crabmeat in my freezer. This recipe made two REALLY BIG crab cakes - crunchy and tasty!
Perfect
Best crab cakes I’ve ever made / eaten!! Fresh crab is a must!
It's very good but I made it my own and put my own twist to it.

Chef John, Did you sneak my crab cake recipe out of my little box. I have used this recipe for years and it never-ever dissapoints. Folks listen to C.John, treat the lump crab carefully. I'm off to the market for Lump Crab. YEP it is that good.
ALL of Chef John's recipes are WINNERS! 🏆
Very bland and the first 2 fell apart. Then I had to add another egg and added breadcrumbs INTO the mix. Would not make again. There are tastier ones out there.
Delicious

This was my first attempt at crab cakes and they were perfect! I was worried that they wouldn't hold together but that just wasn't the case. I'm very proud of myself and thankful that I found chef John
I substituted the crackers with some Melba toast. The rest was perfect.
